policies.title: Kosovo ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Kosovo national travelling on a Kosovo ordinary passport is classified as citizenship, rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: Article 35 says Kosovo citizens may not be denied entry. This does not classify a dual national presenting another country's document.
Residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency-document and final border-admission treatment are outside this classification.

policies.title: Listed foreign ordinary passports: visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo's live MFA schedule names these nationalities as not requiring a short-stay visa, subject to the separately recorded signed amendments and special-document limits.
conditions: This is an ordinary-passport short-visitor classification. The MFA's web contact form and downloadable application do not establish an eVisa, ETA, or visa-on-arrival route.
The Interior Ministry permits a short stay of up to 90 days in every 180 days, subject to a valid travel document, stated purpose, means, address registration, security checks, and final admission.
The MFA separately lists biometric-ID-card and Schengen-document routes. Those document-conditioned exceptions do not broaden this ordinary-passport policy.

Fiji remains unresolved because its later signed amendment makes effectiveness conditional on Gazette publication; Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa are covered by the signed 2024 amendment instead.

policies.title: Hong Kong and Macao travel documents: visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo expressly exempts valid travel documents issued by the Hong Kong and Macao administrations from the visa requirement.
conditions: This is limited to a valid travel document issued by the named administration; it does not make a recognition, citizenship, diplomatic, residence, work, or other-document inference.
The current Interior short-stay and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Taiwan travel documents: visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo exempts Taiwan-issued travel documents, and signed Decision No. 21/216 removes the prior advance-notification condition printed on the live MFA page.
conditions: This is limited to a Taiwan-issued travel document and makes no recognition, citizenship, diplomatic-status, or other-document inference.
A waiver does not remove ordinary travel-document, purpose, means, registration, security, or final-admission checks.

policies.title: Ukraine ordinary passport: temporary visa waiver
policies.summary: Official Gazette Decision No. 14/67 suspends Kosovo's entry-visa regime for Ukrainian citizens until a subsequent Government decision.
conditions: The Gazette states that the waiver remains in force until a later Government decision. No later official revocation was directly retrieved in this review.
This does not establish an eVisa, ETA, arrival-visa, work, residence, or special-document entitlement.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance consular visa required
policies.summary: For these ordinary passports, Kosovo's MFA gives an express visa-required complement and requires an in-person application to the relevant diplomatic or consular mission before a visit or transit.
conditions: The MFA's express complement, not mere omission from a list, supports this baseline. The application must be submitted in person to the relevant Kosovo diplomatic or consular mission; no eVisa, ETA, or nationality-wide arrival-visa route is established.

The published process requires an original application, travel document, purpose, accommodation or means, insurance, and other supporting evidence. Possession of a visa does not automatically confer entry.
A valid biometric Schengen residence permit or valid multiple-entry Schengen visa can create a separate 15-day document-conditioned exemption. It does not change this passport-only baseline.

Russia is expressly excluded from that Schengen-document exception by the Gazette decision. Diplomatic, official, refugee, stateless, UN/NATO/OSCE/EU travel-document, identity-card, residence, work, and transit-specific routes are outside this classification.

application.label: Kosovo short-stay consular visa procedure
application.processingTime: Apply in person no later than three months before the visit; the page publishes no decision-time promise.
steps: Apply in person to the relevant Kosovo diplomatic or consular mission.
Submit the completed original application, travel document, purpose and accommodation or means evidence, insurance, and other requested documents.
Receive the visa decision before travel; possession of a visa does not automatically confer entry.

conflicts.explanation: Signed Decision No. 21/216 places Botswana under Kosovo's visa regime.
Signed Decision No. 21/216 places Namibia under Kosovo's visa regime.

unresolved.reason: Decision No. 02/237 directly establishes Bosnia and Herzegovina entry only with a valid biometric identity card. It does not establish the ordinary-passport baseline, and the MFA complement expressly excludes special categories.

The live MFA schedule still names Fiji visa-free, while signed Decision No. 14/280 adds Fiji to the visa regime only from Official Gazette publication. No Gazette publication or later controlling act was directly retrieved, so the operative ordinary-passport status is not established.

Slovenia is absent from the MFA nationality list but falls within the page's separate EU biometric-ID-card category. That document condition prevents applying the page's ordinary in-person visa complement, and no passport-only rule was directly retrieved.

Kosovo's current MFA page omits Singapore from its named waiver list and gives an express visa-required complement, but current Singapore MFA destination guidance independently states that ordinary Singapore passport holders may visit Kosovo visa-free. No signed Kosovo decision resolving this direct official-source conflict was recovered, so neither status is promoted from this batch.
